question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus washout with chromatin and re-stimulation time course
ideas.description: After a defined AP-1-inducing stimulus, wash it out and track FOS/JUN occupancy (CUT&RUN), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and enhancer marks (H3K27ac) over days. Then re-stimulate and compare the speed and magnitude of target gene induction against naive cells, since faster or stronger re-induction without new AP-1 binding would indicate a memory.

ideas.title: Inducible degradation of AP-1 during and after a priming window
ideas.description: Use an auxin- or dTAG-degradable FOS or JUN allele to remove AP-1 at different times relative to a priming stimulus. Measure whether the memory-like transcriptional and chromatin state persists after AP-1 is gone, which separates AP-1 being required to establish memory from being required to maintain it.

ideas.title: Synthetic tethered AP-1 memory circuit at a reporter locus
ideas.description: Tether engineered AP-1 components (or a dimerized bZIP fusion) to a single-copy reporter with a dox-controlled recruiter, then turn the recruiter off and measure reporter expression, chromatin state, and H3K27ac/H3K4me1 over weeks. Persistence without the tether would show that AP-1 is sufficient to write a self-maintaining state, while mutating its DNA-binding domain would test necessity.

ideas.title: Live single-cell AP-1 reporter tracking across repeated pulses
ideas.description: Track AP-1 activity in individual cells with a live fluorescent reporter during repeated stimulus pulses of varying spacing and strength. Test whether prior pulse history predicts later response magnitude or timing (for example with mutual information or Markov models), and whether this history-dependence is lost when cells are imaged in heterogeneous or lineage-tracked populations.

ideas.title: Pulse-chase protein turnover versus persistence of memory
ideas.description: Use SNAP- or HaloTag-labelled FOS/JUN with pulse-chase labelling to measure AP-1 protein and DNA-bound half-lives in the same cells where memory persists. If memory lasts well beyond AP-1 turnover, combined with mutation of AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers (base editing) and Micro-C or Hi-C for 3D contacts, this would point toward an epigenetic or 3D-architecture-based mechanism rather than a self-sustaining AP-1 feedback loop.
